title: Any signed-in customer can list every customer's personal and payment details
summary: GET /api/admin/customers returns 200 with all customer records (contact name, email, phone, national ID, address, card last 4 digits, internal notes including a card number mentioned in a note) to client accounts. The spec says 401/403 only for admins.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1 (a client account)
GET /api/admin/customers (see evidence for the curl)
Observe HTTP 200 with records of three companies
Repeat as bright-1: same result
actual: HTTP 200 with all customers' personal data for acme-1 and bright-1 (reproduced twice each; anonymous is correctly 401)
suspected_cause: The customers route only checks for a valid sign-in, not the admin role (BFLA, OWASP API5:2023)

regression_test.description: As each client role, GET /admin/customers and expect 403

plain.title: Any customer can see the personal and card details of all other customers
plain.where: Behind the screens (the part that talks to the Client Portal and Admin Portal)
plain.what_happens: A customer who is signed in can ask the system for the full customer list and gets it: names, emails, phone numbers, ID numbers, addresses and card information of every company. Screenshots of this data should be reviewed before sharing.
plain.who_is_affected: Every customer company and the business, which holds their personal data.
plain.expected: Only admins can see the customer list; everyone else is refused.

title: A customer of one company can open another company's order
summary: GET /api/orders/{id} for an order created by acme-1 returns 200 with full contents when requested by bright-1 (a different company). The list endpoint did not show it, so only the detail is unscoped.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1, POST /api/orders with reference QA-rule-at and one line of 80 x p-102; note the order id
Sign in as bright-1 and GET /api/orders/{id}
Observe HTTP 200 and Acme Traders' order
Repeat once more (see evidence)
expected: HTTP 403 or 404 and no order data
actual: HTTP 200 with the order, client name, items and totals (2 of 2). The same order is correctly absent from bright-1's list.
suspected_cause: Order lookup by id does not filter on the caller's company (BOLA, OWASP API1:2023)

regression_test.description: Client A creates an order; client B (other company) GETs it and expects 403/404

plain.title: A customer can open another company's order if they know its number
plain.where: Behind the screens (the part that talks to the Client Portal)
plain.what_happens: An order from Company A can be read in full by a signed-in customer of Company B. The other company's order list correctly does not show it, but the order itself opens.
plain.who_is_affected: Every customer company: their orders, prices and items can be read by competitors.
plain.expected: A customer can only open their own company's orders.

title: Signing out does not end the session: the old sign-in still works
summary: After POST /api/auth/logout returns 204, the same token still gets 200 from GET /api/me.
steps: Sign in over the API as zain-1
POST /api/auth/logout and observe 204
GET /api/me with the same token
Observe HTTP 200 instead of 401 (see evidence for both attempts)
expected: HTTP 401 for the token after logout (config rule: signing out ends the session at once)
actual: HTTP 200 with the user's profile (2 of 2)
suspected_cause: Logout does not revoke the token server-side

regression_test.description: Log out then call /me with the same token and expect 401

plain.title: Signing out does not really sign the person out
plain.where: Behind the screens (the part that talks to the Client Portal and Admin Portal)
plain.what_happens: After someone signs out, their old sign-in still works if it was copied or left on a shared computer. The Sign out button takes them back to the sign-in page, but the access itself is not removed.
plain.who_is_affected: Every user, especially on shared or lost devices.

title: Order tax is calculated on the undiscounted subtotal, so totals are wrong whenever the 5% discount applies
summary: For subtotals of 1,000.00 or more the discount is correct but tax is 10% of the full subtotal instead of the discounted subtotal. Example: 80 x 12.50 = 1,000.00, discount 50.00, tax 100.00 (expected 95.00), total 1,050.00 (expected 1,045.00). Below the threshold (990.99) totals are correct.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1
POST /api/orders reference QA-rule-at with items [{product_id p-102, quantity 80}]
Compare subtotal_cents 100000, discount_cents 5000, tax_cents 10000, total_cents 105000 with expected 100000/5000/9500/104500
Repeat with 80 x p-102 + 2 x p-101 (expected tax about 96.24, got 101.30) and 1000 x p-104
UI: Client Portal New order, 12 x Printer Toner Cartridge shows Total $1,133.88; expected $1,128.47
expected: Total = subtotal - discount + 10% of the discounted subtotal (e.g. 1,045.00 for 1,000.00)
actual: Tax uses the undiscounted subtotal on every order at or above 1,000.00; customers are overcharged about 0.5% (reproduced on 4 orders in the API and in the UI)
suspected_cause: Tax computed from subtotal instead of subtotal minus discount

regression_test.description: Order of 1,000.00 expects discount 50.00, tax 95.00, total 1,045.00; 990.99 expects no discount

plain.title: Customers are overcharged tax on large orders
plain.where: Client Portal → New order → order confirmation, and every order page
plain.what_happens: Orders of 1,000.00 or more get the 5% discount, but tax is still worked out on the price before the discount. Every such order total is too high.
plain.who_is_affected: Customers placing orders of 1,000.00 or more, and the company's sales figures.
how_to_see_it: Sign in to the Client Portal as a customer
Choose Printer Toner Cartridge and set the quantity to 12
Type a reference starting with QA-
You see a total of $1,133.88; with the 5% discount the total should be $1,128.47
plain.expected: Tax is calculated after the discount is taken off.

title: Orders with zero, negative, fractional or too-large quantities, or no items, are accepted
summary: POST /api/orders returns 201 for items = [], quantity 0, 1001, 1.5 and -3. Quantity -3 produces an order with total -21.45 that also appears in the admin list and in sales figures. The spec and config say quantity is a whole number 1-1000 and at least one item.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1
POST /api/orders with items [{product_id p-101, quantity -3}] and reference QA-rule-neg
Observe 201 and total_cents -2145
Repeat for items [] , quantity 0, 1001 and 1.5 (see baseline-client evidence)
actual: HTTP 201 for all five invalid bodies (2 of 2 each)
suspected_cause: No range or integer check on item quantity and no check that items is non-empty

regression_test.description: POST orders with quantity 0, -1, 1001, 1.5 and empty items; expect 400 each

plain.title: The system accepts orders with impossible quantities
plain.where: Behind the screens (the part that talks to the Client Portal)
plain.what_happens: Orders for zero items, minus three items, half an item or more than 1,000 items are accepted, and an order for minus three items has a negative total that is counted in the admin order list and sales numbers.
plain.who_is_affected: Staff reading order totals and the company's sales figures.
plain.expected: The order is refused with a clear message.

title: Order list returns a server error for page_size=0 and for searches containing ( or \, and accepts page_size=-1
summary: GET /api/orders?page_size=0, ?q=( and ?q=\ return HTTP 500 for every role tried; page_size=-1 returns 200 although the spec minimum is 1.
steps: Sign in over the API as admin or acme-1
GET /api/orders?page_size=0
GET /api/orders?q=(
Observe HTTP 500 each time (evidence has the curl)
expected: HTTP 400 for invalid page_size; special characters in search treated as plain text
actual: HTTP 500 (2 of 2 each, as admin and as client)
suspected_cause: page_size not validated; q is probably used unescaped as a regular expression

regression_test.description: GET /orders with page_size 0/-1 expects 400; q='(' expects 200

plain.title: Searching orders with a bracket, or an unusual page size, makes the system fail
plain.where: Behind the screens (the part behind the orders lists)
plain.what_happens: Typing a single bracket or backslash into the order search can make the system fail instead of showing no results.
plain.who_is_affected: Staff and customers searching their orders.
plain.expected: The search shows normal results or an empty list, never an error.

title: Malformed requests return internal technical details (stack trace and file paths)
summary: Malformed JSON sent to POST /auth/login and POST /orders returns 400 with a stack trace, server file paths and a stack field.
steps: POST /api/auth/login with body {bad json
Read the 400 body: it contains a stack trace and server source paths
Repeat on POST /api/orders as acme-1
expected: A short error message without internals
actual: Stack trace and file paths in the response (2 of 2 on both endpoints)
suspected_cause: Default error handler returns the error stack to the client

regression_test.description: Send malformed JSON and assert the body has no 'stack' or file paths

plain.title: Some error messages show the system's internal technical details
plain.where: Behind the screens (the part that talks to the Client Portal)
plain.what_happens: When the system receives a badly formed request, its reply contains internal technical details that help an attacker.
plain.who_is_affected: The business (security exposure); not visible to normal users.
plain.expected: A short, friendly error with no internal details.

title: The customer's orders list keeps showing an old status after an admin changes it
summary: After an admin set QA-ui-order-1 to processing in the Admin Portal, GET /api/orders/{id} shows processing at once but GET /api/orders?q=QA-ui-order-1 (the list) still shows placed for acme-1 and acme-2, still stale about 50 seconds later.
steps: Warm: sign in as acme-1 and view the order in the Client Portal (status placed)
Admin Portal: open the order, choose Processing, click Update status (message confirms)
As acme-1 over the API, GET /orders/{id} -> processing
GET /orders?q=QA-ui-order-1 -> still placed (repeat after ~50 s: still placed)
actual: The list shows the old status; the detail shows the new one (2 of 2 for acme-1 and acme-2)
suspected_cause: A cached orders list per company is not cleared when a status changes (an unwaited cache lifetime may be longer than 50 s)

regression_test.description: Warm list, admin changes status, re-read list and expect new status

plain.title: Customers can keep seeing an out-of-date order status in their orders list
plain.what_happens: After staff move an order forward, the customer's order list can keep showing the old status, even though opening the order shows the new one.
plain.who_is_affected: Customers following their orders; staff who get questions about wrong statuses.
plain.expected: The list shows the new status straight away.

title: Sending an order twice at once creates two identical orders
summary: Two identical simultaneous POST /api/orders were both accepted with 201 (two orders). No idempotency mechanism is documented, so it is unclear whether this is intended; the risk is a customer double-clicking.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1
Send the same POST /api/orders twice at the same moment
Observe two 201 responses with different ids
expected: One order, or a clear duplicate warning (not stated in the spec)
actual: Two orders created (2 of 2); I could not tell whether this is intended

regression_test.description: Parallel identical order POSTs expect a single order

plain.title: A double click on Place order can create two orders
plain.where: Behind the screens (the part that talks to the Client Portal)
plain.what_happens: Two identical orders sent at the same moment both go through. I did not test a real double click on the screen, and it is not stated whether this is wanted.
plain.who_is_affected: Customers who click twice, and staff who must cancel duplicates.
plain.expected: A repeated order is stopped or clearly warned about.

title: The Sales summary report takes about 4 seconds to load
summary: GET /api/admin/reports/sales takes 4003 ms and 4006 ms against a 3000 ms guideline; the Reports page shows only a spinner meanwhile.
steps: Sign in to the Admin Portal
Open Reports
Wait for the spinner (about 4 s); the API call measures 4.0 s on two runs
suspected_cause: A slow query or an artificial delay in the report

plain.title: The Reports page is slow to appear
plain.what_happens: The Sales summary shows a spinner for about four seconds before the numbers appear.
how_to_see_it: Sign in to the Admin Portal as an admin
You see a spinning circle for about four seconds before the numbers appear
plain.expected: The report appears in under three seconds.

title: On a phone, My orders hides the first order and cuts off the Total column
summary: At 390x844 the filter toolbar overlaps the first order row and the table scrolls sideways (474 px inside 359 px) with no visible cue, so Total is cut off.
steps: Sign in to the Client Portal as acme-1
Set the window to 390x844
Open My orders
Observe the first row under the toolbar and totals clipped (second fresh load measured the same numbers)
expected: All rows and totals visible or an obvious way to scroll
actual: First row covered, Total cut off (2 of 2)
suspected_cause: Table wrapper overlaps the toolbar on narrow screens

regression_test.description: At 390px width no element covers the first order row

plain.title: On a phone, the orders list is partly hidden and totals are cut off
plain.what_happens: The first order is covered by the filter bar and the Total column runs off the edge of the screen with no hint to scroll.
how_to_see_it: Sign in to the Client Portal as a customer on a phone-sized screen
You see the first order partly hidden and the totals cut off
plain.expected: Every order and its total can be seen.

title: Some controls have no accessible name (product choice, search box, refresh and clear buttons)
summary: The product dropdown on New order (Client Portal) has no label; on the Admin Orders page the search box has only a placeholder and the refresh and clear-filters icon buttons have no name.
steps: Open Client Portal New order and run the page audit: select[name=product] is unnamed
Open Admin Portal Orders and run the audit at 390x844: input#search, #refresh and #clear-filters are unnamed
Repeat at desktop width (the two icon buttons are also nameless in the page structure)
expected: Every control has a label a screen reader can announce
actual: Four unnamed controls on two pages (2 of 2)

regression_test.description: Accessibility check that no input or button lacks a name

plain.title: Some buttons and fields have no name for screen-reader users
plain.where: Client Portal → New order and Admin Portal → Orders
plain.what_happens: People using screen readers hear nothing meaningful for the product choice box, the search box and two small icon buttons.
plain.who_is_affected: Customers and staff who use screen readers.
plain.expected: Every field and button has a clear name.

title: Urdu order references show their hyphen and digits in a confusing order
summary: References mixing Urdu text and digits (for example the one ending in 1044) are shown in a left-to-right cell and the hyphen and number display scrambled.
steps: Sign in to the Client Portal as the Urdu company's user
Open My orders
Look at the Reference column (page audit lists 3 rows)
expected: The reference reads correctly in order
actual: Hyphen and digits appear in an unexpected visual order (3 of 3 rows; screenshot)
suspected_cause: No dir/bdi isolation for mixed-direction text

regression_test.description: Reference cells use bdi or dir=auto

plain.title: Urdu order numbers look jumbled
plain.what_happens: The order reference, which mixes Urdu letters and numbers, is shown with the dash and digits in a confusing order.
how_to_see_it: Sign in to the Client Portal as the Urdu company's user
